direct_answer:
At year-end 2024, Aker BP’s own workforce comprised 2,962 employees, with a gender split of 2,231 men and 731 women [Source 2]. Employment type disclosures indicate 51 temporary employees and 36 part-time employees [Source 2], and the company states it does not hire employees on zero-hour contracts (i.e., non-guaranteed hours) [Source 6].

Women held 31% of Executive Management Team (EMT) positions at year-end (16 members total) [Source 4].
compliance_rationale: The report provides employee headcount and a gender split (men/women) and gives counts for temporary and part-time employees, plus a statement that there are no zero-hour contracts [Sources 2, 6]. It also provides the percentage of women in the executive management team (31%), enabling the requested percentage for management positions at top management level [Source 4]. However, the ESRS S1-6 requirement for a breakdown by employment type by gender (and explicit permanent vs temporary vs non-guaranteed hours) is not fully met in the retrieved passages, and required methodological notes (headcount vs FTE; point-in-time vs average; and cross-reference to the most representative number in the financial statements) are not provided in the retrieved passages.
disclosure_gaps: Breakdown of employees by employment type (permanent/temporary/non-guaranteed hours) split by gender (e.g., women/men in temporary, part-time, permanent categories).
Explicit number of permanent employees (only implied via total employees and temporary count) and explicit ESRS employment-type categories mapping (permanent, temporary, non-guaranteed hours).
Methodological explanations required by ESRS S1-6 (headcount vs FTE; point-in-time vs average; assumptions/context).

Cross-reference to the most representative workforce number in the financial statements (only a note reference is mentioned without the actual cross-referenced figure in the retrieved passages) [Source 6].
Gender distribution for management beyond EMT (e.g., all management positions definition), if the question is interpreted as broader than top management.
key_findings: Employees at year-end 2024: 2,962; gender split: 2,231 men and 731 women [Source 2].
Employment type indicators: 51 temporary employees and 36 part-time employees; no zero-hour contracts [Sources 2, 6].
Women in top management (Executive Management Team): 31% (16 members total) at year-end [Source 4].
